details.readme:
Everything you need to annotate and stay in the loop with your agents
Inbox Surface • Artifacts • Code Review
Annotate plans, specs, markdown, HTML, and other interactive artifacts. Review diffs and PRs. Send feedback to your agent.

                       

Plannotator Inbox · Official site · Code Review · Visual HTML Skills · Herdr Annotate · (Legacy) Plan Mode

# Plannotator **⭐️ NEW:** [Plannotator Inbox](https://plannotator.ai/inbox/) is the missing review layer between you and multi-agent work. It surfaces decisions, prototypes, variations, plans, and everything you need to stay in the loop. Works with all coding agents and personal assistants. Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface for AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Droid, Amp, DeepSeek Harness, and Pi. Plannotator Inbox also works with personal assistants (Grok Bot, Muse, Hermes, OpenClaw). **It plugs directly into your agent** through plugins, hooks and commands. When the agent proposes a decision, plan, html, or finishes working, the app opens in your browser and you mark it up, comment, and send feedback directly to the agent for it to act on it.
### Review documents, plans, and agent messages Annotate plans, specs, messages, html, then send the feedback to your agent.

Demo: Plan review with Pi
### Code Review Review local changes or remote PRs. Comment on diffs, suggest code. Your comments go back to the agent. Works with Git, GitButler, Jujutsu (`jj`), Perforce (`p4`), GitHub, and GitLab.

AI built in: ask AI about anything you're reviewing,
or launch AI reviews that post comments to the diff.

## Annotate HTML Artifacts

## Plannotator Inbox

The Plannotator Inbox is one local window where your agents leave you messages, questions, files, and guided reviews while they keep working. Answer a question with a click, annotate a file, and press Send when you can. Nothing holds an agent session open while you do, and your reply goes back to the session that asked. ``` plannotator inbox ``` Claude Code, Pi, and OpenCode connect through Plannotator's plugins, and your replies arrive as their next turn. Any other agent reaches it over MCP with `plannotator inbox mcp`, and `plannotator inbox --help` is the guide an agent reads. [Watch the demo](https://plannotator.ai/assets/inbox-film.mp4) · [More on the Inbox](https://plannotator.ai/inbox/) · [Docs](https://plannotator.ai/docs/reference/inbox/) ## Herdr Annotate: Plannotator in the Terminal

  

[Herdr Annotate](https://github.com/plannotator/herdr-annotate) brings Plannotator-style review to the terminal: annotate terminal text, review whole Markdown documents and your coding agent's replies inside [Herdr](https://herdr.dev), and send the feedback straight back to the agent as its next message. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Copilot CLI, and Droid replies. Annotations are saved in the Plannotator data directory, so terminal reviews and app reviews compound. ``` herdr plugin install plannotator/herdr-annotate ``` Prefer it standalone? [Plannotator TUI](https://github.com/plannotator/plannotator-tui) powers the document review and runs without Herdr: `brew install plannotator/tap/plannotator-tui`. --- ## Commands On Codex, swap the slash commands for `!plannotator …` (e.g. `!plannotator review`) or the `$plannotator-*` skills. ### Annotate ``` /plannotator-annotate README.md # Local markdown file /plannotator-annotate src/ # Browse and annotate files in a folder /plannotator-annotate https://docs.rs/… # Fetch and annotate any URL /plannotator-annotate report.html --render-html # Render HTML as-is instead of converting /plannotator-last # Annotate the agent's last message ``` Need a realistic document to try? Copy the [product requirements document template and filled example](https://docs.plannotator.ai/templates/product-requirements-document) as Markdown. ### Code review ``` /plannotator-review # Review uncommitted changes /plannotator-review # Review a GitHub pull request /plannotator-review # Review a GitLab merge request plannotator review --gitbutler # Review an active GitButler workspace plannotator review --patch-file reading.diff # Review a static caller-supplied unified diff ``` GitButler users can review the whole workspace, one stack, or one branch layer. See the [GitButler workflow guide](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/workflows/gitbutler). ### Plan mode No command needed. Plan mode is wired in through each harness's hooks. Any time your agent creates a plan, the markdown review surface opens for you. ### CLI ``` plannotator sessions # List active Plannotator sessions plannotator sessions --open 1 # Reopen a session in the browser plannotator archive # Browse saved plan decisions read-only ``` --- ## Privacy and network behavior Plannotator does not collect usage telemetry or analytics. Plans, diffs, annotations, drafts, history, and configuration stay local by default. Each plan review, annotate, archive, share-portal, and code-review app surface checks GitHub for the latest Plannotator release when it loads. This sends no plan or review content and gives the Plannotator project owner no usage analytics, although GitHub receives an ordinary request. There is currently no opt-out setting for the release check. Local Git code review can also query the configured `origin` with `git ls-remote` to detect the default branch and a stale baseline; it does not send the local diff. That remote query runs when the review opens, when the page loads its diff, when you switch the diff type or base (including the "Diff out of date · Refresh" button), and when you press Fetch — never on a timer, so an idle review page makes no network calls. Turn it off entirely with `plannotator review --no-git-remote-check`, `PLANNOTATOR_GIT_REMOTE_CHECK=0`, or `{ "gitRemoteCheck": false }` in `~/.plannotator/config.json`; the compare target then comes from local refs only and the "behind GitHub" banner never appears. Content leaves the local workflow only when a network feature needs it: - URL annotation fetches the requested site, through Jina Reader by default for public pages or directly when Jina is disabled or unavailable. - GitHub and GitLab review uses your authenticated CLI and Git remote to retrieve PR or MR data. - Ask AI and review agents send the selected question and relevant plan, document, repository, or diff context to your configured provider. When Ask AI is answered by the agent session that opened Plannotator ("Ask this session"), the question goes to that session instead. - Sharing sends the complete link to whoever or whatever service you use to deliver it. Encrypted short links upload ciphertext to the paste service. - Workspaces is a separate hosted product, so the open source app's local-storage model does not apply to content placed there. The [privacy policy](https://plannotator.ai/privacy) documents these boundaries and the hosted website and waitlist data. --- ## Link sharing Open source asynchronous link sharing remains available for compatibility but is moving to deprecated support. Workspaces is the primary direction for team sharing. No removal date has been announced.

Legacy link-sharing demo: room.plannotator.ai

Share a plan with a teammate and they can annotate it themselves. Import their feedback and send it straight back to your agent. **Small markdown shares** are compressed into the URL fragment. The fragment is not included in the browser's request to the share portal, but it is not encrypted. Anyone or any messaging service with the complete link can read the shared content. The portal host still receives ordinary request metadata. **Large markdown and raw HTML shares** use a short-link service. The share payload is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before upload, the server stores only ciphertext, and the key is kept in the URL fragment rather than sent in the paste request. Anyone with the complete link can decrypt it. Hosted pastes expire after 7 days. Same model as [PrivateBin](https://privatebin.info/). The paste service is [self-hostable](https://docs.plan

details.readme:
# Chrome DevTools for agents

[![npm chrome-devtools-mcp package](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/chrome-devtools-mcp.svg)](https://npmjs.org/package/chrome-devtools-mcp)

Chrome DevTools for agents (`chrome-devtools-mcp`) lets your coding agent (such as Antigravity, Claude, Cursor or Copilot)
control and inspect a live Chrome browser. It is available as a
Model-Context-Protocol (MCP) server and as a [CLI][cli]. Both give your AI
coding assistant access to the full power of Chrome DevTools for reliable
automation, in-depth debugging, and performance analysis.

[Tool reference][tool-reference] | [CLI][cli] | [Skills][skills] | [Changelog][changelog] | [Contributing][contributing] | [Troubleshooting][troubleshooting] | [Design Principles][design-principles]

## Key features

- **Get performance insights**: Uses [Chrome
  DevTools](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-frontend) to record
  traces and extract actionable performance insights.
- **Advanced browser debugging**: Analyze network requests, take screenshots and
  check browser console messages (with source-mapped stack traces).
- **Reliable automation**. Uses
  [puppeteer](https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer) to automate actions in
  Chrome and automatically wait for action results.

## Disclaimers

`chrome-devtools-mcp` exposes content of the browser instance to the MCP clients
allowing them to inspect, debug, and modify any data in the browser or DevTools.
Avoid sharing sensitive or personal information that you don't want to share with
MCP clients.

`chrome-devtools-mcp` officially supports Google Chrome and [Chrome for Testing](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-for-testing/) only.
Other Chromium-based browsers may work, but this is not guaranteed, and you may encounter unexpected behavior. Use at your own discretion.
We are committed to providing fixes and support for the latest version of [Extended Stable Chrome](https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule).

Performance tools may send trace URLs to the Google CrUX API to fetch real-user
experience data. This helps provide a holistic performance picture by
presenting field data alongside lab data. This data is collected by the [Chrome
User Experience Report (CrUX)](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/crux). To disable
this, run with the `--no-performance-crux` flag.

## **Usage statistics**

Google collects usage statistics (such as tool invocation success rates, latency, and environment information) to improve the reliability and performance of Chrome DevTools MCP.

Data collection is **enabled by default**. You can opt-out by passing the `--no-usage-statistics` flag when starting the server:

```json
"args": ["-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest", "--no-usage-statistics"]
```

Google handles this data in accordance with the [Google Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy).

Google's collection of usage statistics for Chrome DevTools MCP is independent from the Chrome browser's usage statistics. Opting out of Chrome metrics does not automatically opt you out of this tool, and vice-versa.

Collection is disabled if `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_USAGE_STATISTICS` or `CI` env variables are set.

## Update checks

By default, the server periodically checks the npm registry for updates and logs a notification when a newer version is available.
You can disable these update checks by setting the `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_UPDATE_CHECKS` environment variable.

## Requirements

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) [LTS](https://github.com/nodejs/Release#release-schedule) version.
- [Chrome](https://www.google.com/chrome/) current stable version or newer.
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/)

## Getting started

Add the following config to your MCP client:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "chrome-devtools": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest"]
    }
  }
}
```

> [!NOTE]
> Using `chrome-devtools-mcp@latest` ensures that your MCP client will always use the latest version of the Chrome DevTools MCP server.

### MCP Client configuration

For setup instructions specific to your editor or agent (e.g. Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code), please see our [Client Configurations Guide][client-configurations-guide].

### Your first prompt

Enter the following prompt in your MCP Client to check if everything is working:

```
Check the performance of https://developers.chrome.com
```

Your MCP client should open the browser and record a performance trace.

> [!NOTE]
> The MCP server will start the browser automatically once the MCP client uses a tool that requires a running browser instance. Connecting to the Chrome DevTools MCP server on its own will not automatically start the browser.

## CLI

The package also includes the `chrome-devtools` CLI. Use it to control the browser from your terminal without MCP:

```sh
npm i chrome-devtools-mcp@latest -g
chrome-devtools navigate_page 1 --url "https://developers.chrome.com"
chrome-devtools take_screenshot 1 --filePath screenshot.png
chrome-devtools stop
```

See the [CLI guide][cli] for all commands and options.

## Skills

The package includes [skills](./skills) that teach your agent how to use Chrome DevTools:

| Skill                                                     | Use it to                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| [`chrome-devtools`](./skills/chrome-devtools)             | Debug and automate pages with the MCP tools.    |
| [`chrome-devtools-cli`](./skills/chrome-devtools-cli)     | Run the CLI and write shell scripts with it.    |
| [`a11y-debugging`](./skills/a11y-debugging)               | Audit and fix accessibility issues.             |
| [`cookie-debugging`](./skills/cookie-debugging)           | Debug cookies, sessions, and authentication.    |
| [`debug-optimize-lcp`](./skills/debug-optimize-lcp)       | Debug and improve Largest Contentful Paint.     |
| [`memory-leak-debugging`](./skills/memory-leak-debugging) | Find and fix memory leaks.                      |
| [`troubleshooting`](./skills/troubleshooting)             | Fix connection problems between MCP and Chrome. |

### Install skills as a plugin

A plugin installs the MCP server and all skills, including the CLI skill:

- **Claude Code:** Run `/plugin marketplace add ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp`, then `/plugin install chrome-devtools-mcp@chrome-devtools-plugins`.
- **Copilot / VS Code:** Run **Chat: Install Plugin From Source** and enter `ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp`.
- **Gemini CLI:** Run `gemini extensions install --auto-update https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp`.

See the [Client Configurations Guide][client-configurations-guide] for more information.

### Install skills manually

If your agent does not support plugins, copy the skill folders into the skills directory of your agent. The npm package contains the skills:

```sh
npm i chrome-devtools-mcp@latest -g
# Example for Claude Code. Use the skills directory of your agent.
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
cp -R "$(npm root -g)/chrome-devtools-mcp/skills/chrome-devtools-cli" ~/.claude/skills/
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The `chrome-devtools-cli` skill requires the CLI. Install the package globally before you use the skill.

### Keep skills up to date

Skills describe the tools of a specific version. Update the skills each time you update the MCP server or the CLI. Outdated skills can tell your agent to use tools or parameters that changed.

- **Plugins:** Use the update command of the plugin manager of your agent. The Gemini CLI command above enables automatic updates with `--auto-update`.
- **Manual installs:** Update the package, then copy the skill folders again:

```sh
npm i chrome-devtools-mcp@latest -g
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
cp -R "$(npm root -g)/chrome-devtools-mcp/skills/chrome-devtools-cli" ~/.claude/skills/
```

## Tools

If you run into any issues, checkout our [troubleshooting guide][troubleshooting].
See the full [Tool Reference][tool-reference] for a complete list of all supported MCP capabilities.

## Configuration

Find the complete list of server parameters (e.g., `--headless`, `--isolated`, `--slim`) and how to configure WebSocket connections in the [Configuration Guide][configuration-guide].

For basic browser tasks only, the `--slim` flag exposes a reduced set of tools. See the [Slim tool reference][slim-tool-reference].

## Advanced Usage

For advanced features such as handling concurrent sessions, persistent user data directories, using a custom or non-standard browser path (`--executablePath`), connecting to a running Chrome instance instead of starting a new one, or debugging on Android, see our [Advanced Usage Guide][advanced-usage-guide].

## Integrating as a browser subagent

If you are developing agentic tooling and want to provide an integrated browser subagent as part of your product, we recommend building on top of Chrome DevTools for agents.

For a reference implementation, see the [Gemini CLI browser agent documentation](https://geminicli.com/docs/core/subagents/#browser-agent).

repository.description: Self-hosted workflows for coding-agent delivery. Orchestrate CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code with scripts and human approval gates. Includes Local workflows for coding assistants.

details.readme:
English · 简体中文

Two ways to work · Quick start · SOPs · Features · Local · FAQ · Docs

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8af401d9-1aae-427c-b4bc-455c12d17beb

80-second product tour (1080p, with sound).

**LoopForge** is a self-hosted workspace where your team ships software with coding agents. Describe what you need to **Main Bot** in chat: it opens a Docker sandbox, checks out your repositories, delegates to project roles, and opens the PR. When a way of working proves itself, save it as an **SOP** (a standard workflow of agents, scripts and human gates) so the next requirement is delivered the same way, with review and approval built in. Coding-agent CLIs do the work: CodeBuddy, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Antigravity, Kimi Code, Pi, DeepSeek Harness and ZCode. LoopForge adds the roles, sandboxes, checkpoints and history around them, all on your own infrastructure under the MIT license. ## Two ways to work | | **Chat with Main Bot** | **Run an SOP** | | --- | --- | --- | | Best for | Exploring, quick fixes, iterating with the agent | Repeatable delivery with fixed stages and sign-off | | How it runs | Main Bot opens a [conversation workspace](docs/conversation-workspaces.md) (a Docker sandbox with your repos) on demand and calls project roles as subagents | The engine runs Agent, Script, Human-gate and sub-SOP nodes in order, in their own sandbox | | You stay in control by | Queuing or steering messages mid-reply, and pausing, resuming or taking over a running SOP from chat | Approving at human gates, sending work back to a chosen step, retrying or rerunning from any node | | Delivers | A PR/MR, or a direct merge into a shared branch (`mode=direct`) | Documents, code or a PR, plus per-node artifacts and logs | Both paths track the same **requirements**, so every change, whether made in chat or by an SOP, links back to what was asked for and counts toward delivery and cost reports.

The chat home. Type a request, @ a role, skill, requirement, SOP or repository, and pick the executor, model and permission mode per conversation.

## Why LoopForge Ask a coding agent to "fix this bug" and the result depends on that run. It might skip the plan, forget the tests, review its own code, or stop halfway without anyone noticing. That's fine for a demo, but it isn't how a team ships. - **Repeatable.** Same SOP, same stages, same checks for every requirement. Start from built-in backend, frontend, bug-fix and product SOPs. - **Separated roles.** Planning, implementation, review and testing each get their own prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools. A role works as an SOP node or as a subagent in chat. - **Human in the loop.** Approval gates where they matter. Read the report, approve, or send the work back to a chosen step. - **Observable and resumable.** Node status, tool traces, logs and artifacts in one place. Pause, retry a failed step, or rerun from any node. - **Your stack, your servers.** Ten coding-agent CLIs as executors, from CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code to OpenCode, Cursor CLI and more. GitHub, Skills and MCP as tools. Docker sandboxes or your own machine as the runtime. ## Quick start Install **Git** and clone the repository first. The installer checks Docker, Compose, Python 3 and curl and offers to install missing components. Python/curl installation supports apt, dnf and yum on Linux; the Compose plugin supports x86_64/arm64 and verifies the official release SHA-256. macOS needs a working Python 3 and Docker Desktop; Homebrew can install missing components. Ordinary Linux users are supported through Docker group access or sudo. Set `LOOPFORGE_YES=1` to accept installation prompts. Package and image downloads require internet access. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Tencent/LoopForge.git cd LoopForge ./start.sh ``` `./start.sh` pulls the GHCR release image pinned in `compose.yaml` without building locally (`bash scripts/install.sh` does the same). It creates the MySQL and platform services, generates configuration and session secrets, and installs the built-in sandboxes, starter SOPs and welcome project. Host Go and Node.js installations are not required. Configure model API keys and GitHub authorization after startup. Use `./start.sh logs`, `stop`, `restart` or `pull` to manage it, and `./start.sh dev` to build the checkout from source. If downloads from `ghcr.io` stall, set `MIRROR` to a registry host that can stand in for `ghcr.io`. `./start.sh` pulls from that host and tags the image back to the name pinned in `compose.yaml`. Setting `MIRROR` trusts that host, because the download is tagged with the official name. The GitHub Release records the digest; `docker image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' ghcr.io/tencent/loopforge:` should show the same digest after `@`. Without `MIRROR`, `./start.sh` still pulls `ghcr.io` directly, and `compose.yaml` stays unchanged. Upgrade with the same variable and `./start.sh pull`. [ghcr.nju.edu.cn](https://doc.nju.edu.cn/books/e1654/page/ghcr) is one such host. A Docker `registry-mirrors` entry such as `https://docker.nju.edu.cn` only accelerates Docker Hub and is not a value for `MIRROR`. ```bash MIRROR=ghcr.nju.edu.cn ./start.sh ``` Open the address printed by the installer and create your account; the first one becomes the administrator. The service listens on `0.0.0.0:8090` by default. On a cloud host, the installer reads the public IP from the provider's metadata service and prints it; allow the port in your security group, or put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front. Restrict access to your own IP until the administrator account exists. The home page's quick-access guide walks you through adding a model key, connecting a repository and choosing an SOP. For GitLab, Gitea, Gogs and other Git hosts, [set up Git SSH](docs/deployment.md#git-repositories-over-ssh) to check out and push branches with a personal key. PR/MR and Issue automation requires a hosting API token or a separately configured MCP. ### Try it without an API key New accounts join the **LoopForge demo project**, which includes an SOP made only of a script and a human gate: 1. Switch to the demo project, open **Templates**, and open **Platform check · script & approval**. 2. Click **Run SOP**. A real script writes a report, then the run waits for you at the approval step. 3. Approve it from **Needs review** or the run page, and watch the run continue to its final artifact. ### What you need for real work | I want to… | You need | | --- | --- | | Run the script + approval demo | Nothing | | Chat with Main Bot, generate a document or a new project | An API key for the selected executor | | Change an existing repository (in chat or via an SOP) and open a PR | Model credentials and a GitHub repository (connect GitHub in personal settings) |
More setup details: executors, GitHub, sandboxes, access model
- **Executors.** Pick one of ten CLIs beside the home composer, then a model. Every SOP role can choose its executor independently (built-in roles default to CodeBuddy). Requirement clarification, AI notification summaries, Bot replies and run evals currently use CodeBuddy, so their model pickers list CodeBuddy models only and the server refuses a model of another CLI instead of switching it to CodeBuddy; scheduled assistant tasks run on the CLI the task selects. | Executor | Credentials | Installation | | --- | --- | --- | | **CodeBuddy** | Personal key, or a shared key an administrator configures for chat and SOP runs | In the Docker image | | **Codex** | Personal key; a connected execution machine can use its local login | In the Docker image | | **Claude Code** | Personal key; a connected execution machine can use its local login | Installed from npm on first use, then cached | | **OpenCode · Kimi Code · Pi** | Personal key only | Installed from npm on first use, then cached | | **DeepSeek Harness** | Personal key only | In the Docker image | | **Cursor CLI · Antigravity** | Personal key only | Provider installer on first chat use; not installed into SOP sandboxes | | **ZCode** | Personal key only | Not bundled; install it on the service or execution machine PATH | The seven agent CLIs after Claude Code keep their model and MCP configuration in a private home directory per run, so they always use the responsible user's own key and Base URL from personal settings, even on a connected execution machine. When rolling them out to a team, each member configures their own credentials. First-use installs need npm or provider access; [native deployments](docs/deployment.md#workers-and-runners) need the CLI for the executor you choose. - **GitHub is optional.** All built-in generic SOPs run without a repository: product SOPs deliver documents, and new frontend/backend projects deliver source files in the task workspace. Bug fixes still need source code and reproduction details. Connect a repository when you work on existing code or want PRs. - **Delivering to a repository.** Choose **Connect GitHub** in personal settings, approve the device code on GitHub and pick your repository (the LoopForge OAuth App is built in; no PAT required, manual PAT entry still works). Set executor credentials (or bind a local execution machine), then either run a project SOP or ask Main Bot to change the code and submit a PR/MR. - **Sandboxes.** In the default Compose installation, SOP runs and conversation workspaces both use Docker sandbox containers started through the host Docker socket. Default sandboxes reuse the installed runtime image, so nothing extra is built after installation; custom Dockerfiles stil

repository.description: Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

details.readme:
Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Studio | Quickstart | Showcase | Playground | Catalog | Docs | Discord

Download the desktop app: macOS · Windows · Linux (.deb)

HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. The [HyperFrames Studio app](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/studio-app) is free to use as well; its [Pro plan](https://hyperframes.studio/pricing) adds HeyGen's top video, image, voice and music models. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Without the picker (a script or a CI job), `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 9 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs the skills from the release tag that matches your CLI version, so they match the CLI that runs them. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 9 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`, `/reverse-any-video`, `/style-sampling`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 9. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow` and `/remotion-to-hyperframes` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Plugin packages Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager. `bun run package:agent-plugin` builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata, and SHA-256 checksum. See the [maintainer checklist](docs/contributing/agent-plugins.mdx). ### Upload to Codex Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed `HEAD` version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills: ```bash bun run package:codex-plugin ``` This writes `dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip` with a `hyperframes/` root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit. ### Core set | Skill | Use when | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/hyperframes` | **Read first** for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards. | | `/hyperframes-cli` | The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, share, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures. | | `/hyperframes-registry` | About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for `hyperframes add` and `catalog`. | | `/media-use` | Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull. | | `/reverse-any-video` | Rebuilding any video file as an editable HyperFrames project (motion graphics, talking heads, live action, AI-generated footage), checked frame by frame against the original. HyperFrames Pro. | | `/style-sampling` | Making a new episode on your topic in one of five proven styles: Collage Explainer, Finance Explainer, Animated Science Explainer, 3D Brand Explainer, 3D True Crime. HyperFrames Pro. | ### On demand | Skill | Use when | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/figma` | Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link. | | `/slideshow` | A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4. | | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` | Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame. | For visual design handoff workflows, see the [Claude Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/design-tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme#start-from-claude-design-or-open-design) and [Open Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/design-tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme#start-from-claude-design-or-open-design). ### Manually with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` **Requirements:** Node.js 22+, FFmpeg ## What You Can Build Need ideas? repository.description: Run the original Windows releases of visual novels on Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android.

details.readme:
Hitode

Run the original Windows releases of visual novels on Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android.
English · 简体中文

> [!IMPORTANT] > Hitode is experimental. Only a few engines and games have been adapted and tested so far. It is not ready for everyday play yet: expect crashes, missing features and breaking changes. How many steps does it take to put an elephant in a fridge? Open the door, put it in, close the door. Hitode wants playing a visual novel on a Mac or a mobile device to take three steps as well: pick the game folder, press Start, play. ## Features **One runtime for the common ARM platforms** - macOS (Apple silicon), iOS / iPadOS and Android share one runtime. Its own x86 → ARM64 JIT translates game code straight into ARM64 machine code with no intermediate representation, so one optimization helps all three platforms. - Graphics use each platform's native API, Metal on Apple platforms and Vulkan on Android, with power-saving work such as damage-based drawing. **Compatible with the original games** - The original exe, DLLs and translation patches run directly. No port is needed, and no particular engine is assumed. - Hitode does not rebuild all of Windows. It implements the system features visual novels actually use, faithful to how Windows defines them. Fixes go into that shared behavior, so every game adapted helps the next game that needs the same feature. - Patch-friendly: translation patches often rewrite import tables, function prologues or COM vtables. Every fast path detects such rewrites and falls back to the general path, so the patch still takes effect. - Text encoding is detected per game (Japanese / Simplified Chinese). Bundled videos, disc images (up to four mounted ISOs) and font substitution work as well. **Player** For now Hitode ships a simple player: a launcher that manages the library (with [VNDB](https://vndb.org/) metadata and play time) and keeps per-game settings; upscaling filters such as Anime4K and CuNNy; and controls adapted to mobile devices and the Mac.

## Which games run Hitode does not target particular games or engines. It implements the system features 32-bit Windows visual novels commonly use: GDI, DirectDraw, Direct3D 9, DirectSound, DirectInput, and video through DirectShow, Windows Media and VfW. A game built on these has a chance to run as it is, whether it uses a commercial engine, any version of one, or a brand's in-house engine. Not supported: 64-bit programs; programs that use Direct3D 10 or later, or OpenGL; programs that only run after bypassing a protector or DRM. To find out whether your game runs, import it and try. If it will not start, freezes, crashes, stutters or drains the battery, [tell us](https://github.com/hitode-project/hitode/issues/new?template=game-issue.yml) which game and what happened, ideally with the anonymous report the launcher creates. Issues with the same cause are grouped together, and the fix goes into the shared behavior, so one fix helps every similar game. Known problems are in the [issue list](https://github.com/hitode-project/hitode/issues?q=label%3Acompatibility); share the games that play well in [Discussions](https://github.com/hitode-project/hitode/discussions). ## Platforms | Platform | Status | Notes | |---|---|---| | macOS (Apple silicon) | Supported | | | Android (ARMv8-A, 64-bit) | Supported | | | iOS / iPadOS | Supported | Targets iOS / iPadOS 16.2 and later on A12 or newer. Sideloading and JIT setup depend on the system version. See [the iOS guide](docs/ios.zh-CN.md) (Chinese) | ## Download Builds for each platform are on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/hitode-project/hitode/releases). ## How it works Hitode has two parts: a **runtime** that runs Windows programs, and a **player** that hosts it on each platform. The approach follows console emulators: the game's own code runs unchanged, and Hitode provides the "hardware" it expects, namely a subset of Windows, graphics, audio and video devices, time and threads. Windows behavior comes from Wine, built together with the rest of Hitode; its modules run as guest code and cover the long tail. Everything the player feels is host code: audio mixing, MIDI, video decoding, DirectDraw and Direct3D 9, and the timing of all of them. The NT kernel, the Wine server and the drivers run in the same process, so the layers call each other directly. Where a Wine function's bytes are verified unchanged, a native body may run it as host code with the same result. The runtime also runs without the launcher. `adv-run` is its command-line entry point, for debugging and automated tests. [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) maps the code: which layers exist, how they connect and where to look for details. The rules every part must follow are in [docs/spec/](docs/spec/README.md), and switches and options are listed in [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md). ## How it compares | | Kirikiroid2, ONScripter and similar | Winlator, CrossOver and similar | Hitode | |---|---|---|---| | Games | Specific engines | Most Windows programs | 32-bit visual novel engines | | Needs a port | Often | No | No | | Original and translation patches | Depends on the port | Yes | Yes | | Setup | Easy | Versions and settings often tuned per game | Pick a folder | | Audio and video | Native in the port | Wine's general-purpose drivers | Native on the host | Hitode sits between the two: it loads the original program and patches as they are, takes the long tail of Windows behavior from Wine, and runs audio, video and graphics, the parts players feel directly, natively on the host. Every part is built and released together, so a compatibility problem is fixed once, in code, for every game and platform, without per-game settings. ## Building You need stable Rust and Python 3; the launcher also needs Node.js and pnpm, and video playback needs FFmpeg 8. ```sh cargo build --release -p adv-run ./target/release/adv-run --help ``` The launcher, builds with media, the player on each platform and macOS packaging are covered in [docs/building.md](docs/building.md). Neither the repository nor any build contains game files. ## Contributing Feedback and contributions are welcome: - **Game problems**: use the "game issue" template, naming the game and what happens; the report the launcher saves helps. Search for the game first, and reply there if it is already reported. - **Player (launcher UI, new features)**: the launcher is still simple, which makes it the easiest place to start. Issues and pull requests are welcome. - **Runtime: engine and game support**: changes go into the shared Windows behavior, never workarounds for a single game. Each behavior implemented helps every game that uses it, so supporting the next game keeps getting cheaper. - **Runtime: performance**: optimizations of the CPU, devices and presentation are welcome. - **Changes across layers or to a contract** (contracts are in [docs/spec/](docs/spec/README.md)): please open an issue to discuss first. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before you start. Do not commit files, screenshots or traces of commercial games. ## Acknowledgements Hitode would not exist without these projects. **Runtime** - [Wine](https://www.winehq.org/): Windows behavior comes from its modules, which run as guest code, and its server runs inside Hitode. Its source and tests have long been our main reference for how Windows behaves. - [FreeType](https://freetype.org/): rasterizes the games' text. - [iced-x86](https://github.com/icedland/iced): the x86 decoder under our CPU. - [Unicorn](https://www.unicorn-engine.org/) and [QEMU](https://www.qemu.org/): the reference CPUs our tests compare against. - [SingleStepTests/80386](https://github.com/SingleStepTests/80386): per-instruction test vectors. - [Berkeley SoftFloat](http://www.jhauser.us/arithmetic/SoftFloat.html): the basis of our x87 floating point. - Microsoft's [Win32Metadata](https://github.com/microsoft/win32metadata) provides the API signatures; the hook tests use [Detours](https://github.com/microsoft/Detours) and [MinHook](https://github.com/TsudaKageyu/minhook). **Player** - [StikDebug](https://github.com/StikDebug/StikDebug) and [idevice](https://github.com/jkcoxson/idevice): JIT on iPhone and iPad without a computer. - [Moonlight](https://moonlight-stream.org/): the timing of our touch gestures follows its implementation. - [Magpie](https://github.com/Blinue/Magpie): our upscaling shaders are ported from it; the originals are [Anime4K](https://github.com/bloc97/Anime4K), [CuNNy](https://github.com/funnyplanter/CuNNy), [ArtCNN](https://github.com/Artoriuz/ArtCNN) and k7_modernAnime from [mpv_PlayKit](https://github.com/hooke007/mpv_PlayKit). - [OxiSynth](https://github.com/PolyMeilex/OxiSynth) and the FluidR3 Mono SoundFont: MIDI music synthesis. - [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/) and Xiph's [libtheora](https://www.theora.org/): playback of the games' own videos. We also use [Symphonia](https://github.com/pdeljanov/Symphonia), [cpal](https://github.com/RustAudio/cpal), [encoding_rs](https://github.com/hsivonen/encoding_rs), [corosensei](https://github.com/Amanieu/corosensei), [Tauri](https://tauri.app/) and [Svelte](https://svelte.dev/). The name comes from the wooden starfish (*hitode*) that Fuko Ibuki carves one by one and gives to everyone in *CLANNAD*. We want to hand these old games, one by one, to more people too. ## Disclaimer Hitode is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by the developers or rights holders of any game engine or game, or any other trademark or copyright owner mentioned here. All trademarks belong to their respective owners. Hitode contains no game data. Please use copies of games you obtained legally. ## License Copyright © 2026 [ttyymm233](https://github.com/ttyymm233) and the Hitode contributors. Hitode is releas

details.readme:
# Phosphene: free local AI video generator for Mac **Phosphene is a free, open-source Mac app that makes AI video with sound, pictures, songs and speech on your own Apple Silicon Mac.** It runs LTX-2.5, MiniMax H3 (Hailuo H3) and MiniMax-H3-Image locally with MLX: offline, no cloud, no API key, no account, no NVIDIA GPU. **Current release: v5.0.26.** Mac app or Pinokio · M1 to M5 · from 16 GB of memory · MIT licence · made by Mr Bizarro

Download for Mac · See every feature · Will my Mac run it? · Docs

## At a glance - **What it makes:** text-to-video and image-to-video with sound, lip-sync, long single shots, multi-shot films, an editing timeline, AI images and image editing, songs with vocals, text to speech, trained characters. - **Models:** LTX-2.5 (Lightricks), MiniMax H3 / Hailuo H3, MiniMax-H3-Image, P-H3-Image, FLUX.2 [klein], FLUX 3 Klein, Qwen-Image-Edit, Ideogram 4, YuE2, Qwen3-TTS, Gemma. - **Runs on:** Apple Silicon Macs, M1 to M5, from 16 GB of unified memory. Not Intel Macs, not Windows. - **Installs as:** a native Mac app, or one click through Pinokio. - **Costs:** free, with no credits, watermark or per-render charge. Optional Pro funds the project. - **Privacy:** renders on your Mac. Prompts, pictures and videos are never uploaded. ## What you can make ### Video with sound: LTX-2.5 on Apple Silicon Turn a prompt or a picture into a clip whose picture and sound are generated together, using the MLX port of Lightricks' LTX-2.5. Modes: **Text**, **Image** (animate your picture, or take its character into a new shot), **Start & end frame**, **Keyframes** (3 to 8 frames), **Extend**, **Lip-sync** to your own voice or song, and **Remix**: **Motion Control** copies the motion and camera of a clip you give it ([guide](docs/MOTION_CONTROL.md)), **Ingredients** combines 2 to 8 reference pictures, **Colorize** turns black-and-white footage into colour, and **Upscale & Face Fix** sharpens a finished clip. LTX-2.5 works from 16 GB of memory at smaller sizes and at full size from 48 GB. Since 5.0.20 a video on a 16 GB Mac peaks at about 5.7 GB of memory (it was 9 GB), and a render with LoRAs at about 6.7 GB (it was 19 GB), with the same frames as before.

“Stone eye, gold tear” (image to video) and “The Drowned Ballroom” (text to video), LTX-2.5. Every clip on this page was rendered on one Mac with Phosphene.

### People who talk: MiniMax H3 (Hailuo) locally on a Mac MiniMax H3, also called Hailuo H3, is Phosphene's second video engine, for scenes where people speak: dialogue, voices and sound come out of one pass, with lips that match. It does text and image to video, start and end frames, keyframes, Extend up to 15 seconds, lip-sync, and **Add sound**, which gives a silent clip its own soundscape. Since 5.0.7 it runs from **16 GB** of memory: Draft and Standard from 16 GB, High from 18 GB; Clean up sound and 10 and 15-second chained clips need 36 GB. It is an optional download of about 75 GB (allow about 100 GB free while it installs), inside the Mac app or from the Pinokio sidebar. Its licence does not cover the EU, the UK, South Korea or the US.

“The mirror blinks late” and “The low-tide sleeper”, MiniMax H3, image to video

### Films: One Shot, Storyboard and the Editor - **One Shot:** one continuous shot of 30 seconds to 2 minutes that never cuts. - **Storyboard:** describe a film in a sentence; a local model writes the shot list, you edit it, draft every shot small and fast, then finish only the takes you keep. Add a song and it cuts a music video to the beat. - **Editor:** a real timeline with trims, splits, J and L cuts, music, titles and transitions. Render one file, or export the timeline to DaVinci Resolve, Premiere Pro or After Effects. - **Make it vertical:** a 9:16, 4:5 or square copy of any clip, in the More menu.

The Editor: takes from any engine on one timeline, with their own sound, music and room tone.

### Pictures and image editing: MiniMax-H3-Image and more The Images tab makes stills and edits them in plain words, then sends any picture straight to video. - **MiniMax-H3-Image** (MiniMax): detailed pictures from a descriptive prompt at 4, 8 or 16 megapixels. **New in 5.0.19, it edits your pictures:** drop a photo in, say what to change, combine up to 6 pictures in one edit, or change the shape and let it fill the new area. Free, a preview; needs Hailuo H3 installed. - **P-H3-Image** (Pruna AI, built on MiniMax H3): large photographs and posters with words spelled right. - **FLUX.2 [klein]**, the light first model, and **FLUX 3 Klein** (Black Forest Labs): pictures from words or from your reference pictures. - **Reference Edit** (Qwen-Image-Edit): change a background or an outfit, or combine up to three references. - **Ideogram 4:** readable words placed where you want them on a picture.

Combining pictures with MiniMax-H3-Image: Picture 1 (the street) plus Picture 2 (the man) becomes one photograph. About 8 minutes for two pictures at Draft on an M4 Max with 64 GB.

### Songs, speech and lip-sync - **Music Studio** writes a full song with vocals and instruments from your lyrics and a style with YuE2, or an instrumental. Make another take, cover a song, or get the score. About 11 GB, from 16 GB of memory. - **Speech** turns a script into a spoken voice with Qwen3-TTS: nine preset voices with a delivery you describe, or a voice you have permission to use. About 6 GB, from 16 GB of memory. - **Lip-sync** makes a face in a picture talk or sing to your track, on LTX-2.5 or MiniMax H3.

“Neon Mile”, a Music Studio song sung with MiniMax H3, and “The bust sings”, LTX-2.5 lip-sync

### Characters and LoRAs Train a character LoRA on your Mac from 15 to 50 of your own photos, of an original character or of yourself, then put it in any LTX shot. Gemma writes the training captions locally. Training needs 24 GB; the graded High recipe runs on 64 GB or more. Browse and install LTX and H3 LoRAs inside the app. ## Mac requirements **Will it run on your Mac?** The full answer for every memory size, with measured clip times per chip: [phosphene.video/mac-requirements](https://phosphene.video/mac-requirements/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=install). Any Apple Silicon Mac from M1 to M5: MacBook Air, MacBook Pro, iMac, Mac mini, Mac Studio. Memory decides what you can run, and Phosphene only offers what your Mac can handle. | Memory | What you can make | | --- | --- | | **16 GB** | LTX-2.5 video at smaller sizes, MiniMax H3 Draft and Standard (High from 18 GB), FLUX.2 [klein] pictures, songs, speech | | **24 GB** | Also image editing with Reference Edit, FLUX 3 Klein and Ideogram 4, and character training | | **32 GB** | Also P-H3-Image | | **36 GB** | Also MiniMax-H3-Image, long chained H3 clips and Clean up sound | | **48 to 64 GB** | Also LTX-2.5 at full size, High quality, Keyframes, Extend, trained characters | | **96 GB and up** | Larger keyframe and extend sizes; no size limits from 120 GB | **Disk:** setup itself downloads no models and needs 18 GB free. LTX-2.5 video is about 27.5 GB; MiniMax H3 about 75 GB; songs about 11 GB; speech about 6 GB; image models download on first use. In the Mac app the models can live on an external drive: choose the folder at setup or later in Settings. The [Mac requirements page](https://phosphene.video/mac-requirements/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=website&utm_content=requirements) answers it for your exact chip and memory, with render times measured on Macs like yours. ## Install **Mac app (recommended):** [download Phosphene for Mac](https://phosphene.video/download/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=install&utm_content=mac-app), open it, review the setup plan, and pick the models you want. It updates itself, and it reuses models a Pinokio install already downloaded. **Pinokio:** Phosphene also installs with one click through [Pinokio](https://pinokio.computer), a free app launcher: 1. Install Pinokio. 2. Open **Discover → Download from URL** and paste `https://github.com/mrbizarro/phosphene`. 3. Press **Install**, then **Start**, then open the app. To update in Pinokio, press **Update**, then restart Phosphene. The [install guide](https://phosphene.video/docs/install/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=docs&utm_content=install) covers disk space, updates and troubleshooting. To install by hand, follow the [manual install](docs/MANUAL_INSTALL.md). Linux on Apple Silicon ([`docs/LINUX.md`](docs/LINUX.md)) is a community port maintained by @joshuaswarren on a best-effort basis. ## iPhone Remote **Phosphene Remote** is the iPhone app that drives your Mac's studio: write prompts, run every Studio workflow, watch progress and save finished clips to your phone, at home or away. The Mac does the rendering. It is part of Pro: a Pro licence turns it on.
